verdict_namespace_note: The prompt's RACE_STAGE1_* namespace is already used by the unrelated stage3_residency/stage1_prediction study in this repository. The verdict token is renamed to OSM_STAGE1_* (Optimizer-State Memory) and is reported together with its RACE_STAGE1_* equivalent so either name resolves to the same single verdict.

stage_scope.purpose: Determine whether optimizer-state memory under continual test-time adaptation is a real, causal, shift-dependent phenomenon.
forbidden_in_this_stage: designing, implementing, tuning or evaluating a new optimizer
optimizing any method to beat TTA baselines

hypotheses.H1_boundary_state: After an abrupt shift, carrying Adam state from domain A into domain B produces measurably different early adaptation from starting B with modified/reset optimizer state, holding model parameters identical.
hypotheses.H2_shift_specificity: Any reset benefit is substantially larger after a true domain change than at a stationary pseudo-boundary.
hypotheses.H3_first_moment: Lower / more negative cos(m_previous, g_current) at the boundary predicts greater benefit from removing old first-moment information.
hypotheses.H4_memory_timescale: Sensitivity to first-moment reset weakens as beta1 -> 0 and strengthens as beta1 -> 1.
hypotheses.H5_state_component: First moment, second moment and the step/bias-correction counter contribute differently and must be manipulated separately.

benchmark.arch_primary_description: RobustBench WideResNet-28-10, the default model of the official Tent CIFAR-10-C example
benchmark.arch_secondary_description: WRN-40-2, the second model of the same official example; used only to resolve which reference error rates apply
benchmark.adaptation: Tent entropy minimisation, BatchNorm2d affine scale/shift only
benchmark.prediction_semantics: predict -> record prediction -> entropy -> backward -> optimizer step; the recorded prediction is the pre-update one

baseline_validity.prompt_reference_note: The ~18.3% / ~12.1% figures quoted in the task brief are the WRN-40-2 AugMix row of the official Tent README, not the WRN-28-10 row. The WRN-28-10 primary model is validated against 43.5 / 20.4 / 18.6.
baseline_validity.rule: If the reproduced mean corruption error differs from the matching official reference by more than 2.0 percentage points and the discrepancy cannot be explained, declare BASELINE_INVALID and make no scientific claims from later experiments.

primary_outcome.name: early10_accuracy
primary_outcome.definition: mean online top-1 accuracy over the first 10 adaptation batches after a boundary, pre-update predictions, batch size 200 (first 2000 post-boundary samples)
primary_outcome.effect: reset_benefit = early10_accuracy(intervention) - early10_accuracy(CARRY_ALL), in percentage points

recovery_time_rule.plateau: accuracy of the CARRY_ALL branch over the last 10 batches of its own post-boundary window
recovery_time_rule.statistic: smallest k >= 1 such that the mean accuracy of batches k..k+4 is >= threshold
recovery_time_rule.note: the threshold is shared by all branches at a boundary so branches are comparable

primary.name: matched_branch_boundary
primary.trajectory: one continual Tent chain per (corruption order, seed) starting from the source checkpoint; the chain itself is standard continual Tent (CARRY_ALL)
primary.branching: at every domain boundary the exact model checkpoint and the exact optimizer snapshot are cloned into all six interventions; every branch starts domain B with bitwise-identical model weights and consumes the identical domain-B batches in identical order

stationary_control.name: matched_pseudo_boundary
stationary_control.description: At the mid-point of each domain (after 25 Adam updates inside the domain) the identical checkpoint is branched twice: once onto the held-out second half of the SAME corruption (stationary) and once onto the first half of the NEXT corruption (shifted). Both conditions share the same checkpoint, the same optimizer history and the same number of Adam updates; only the incoming distribution differs.

beta1_sweep.note: beta1=0.9 is shared with the primary run and is re-run inside the sweep so the sweep is internally matched

lr_sweep.note: 3e-3 only if stable; instability is reported, not silently dropped

statistics.experimental_unit: transition = (corruption order, boundary index); seeds are replicates within a transition
statistics.aggregation: mean over seeds within a transition, then bootstrap over transitions

association.primary: Spearman rho between boundary cos(m,g) and reset_benefit(RESET_M_KEEP_V_STEP)

statistics.outlier_rule: No transition is removed for any reason. Every tested transition, including negative results, is stored and reported.
statistics.nonparametric_test: paired Wilcoxon reported as a secondary descriptor only

STRONG_GO: at least one moment intervention improves early10_accuracy over CARRY_ALL by >= 1.0 percentage point on average (or produces a comparably meaningful transient improvement)
effect present in >= 70% of tested abrupt transitions
true-shift benefit substantially larger than the stationary pseudo-boundary benefit
RESET_STEP_ONLY does not explain most of the effect
at least one mechanistic signature supports the hypothesis (cos(m,g) predicts benefit, or sensitivity grows with beta1)
WEAK_GO: reproducible effects of roughly 0.5-1.0 percentage point
only a subset of shifts shows the phenomenon
mechanistic relationship suggestive but not strong
NO_GO: resets help equally in stationary conditions
optimizer-state diagnostics show no meaningful relationship with adaptation behaviour
go_no_go.reverse_result_rule: If carried optimizer state consistently HELPS after shifts, that result is preserved and reported as-is. The scientific objective is to understand when optimizer memory helps versus hurts; the desired conclusion is not predetermined.

label_policy: Target labels are used for evaluation only. They never enter adaptation, optimizer-state decisions, gradient diagnostics, or any hyper-parameter choice. Corruption identities and boundary locations are used only as oracle diagnostics and every such experiment is tagged ORACLE_BOUNDARY_DIAGNOSTIC.
